title: KENREX by Jack Holden and Ed Stambollouian at the Lucille Lortel Thea...
transcript: This astonishing solo play about a Missouri criminal is a must-see. Jack Holden, who just won an Olivier for this show in London, tells a true story in a remarkably transformative fashion. He embodies over 30 different characters, tapping into specific voices and physicalities for each one. This show is not very concerned with telling the story efficiently, but rather letting it unfold in a textured and investigative way. The world building that Jack does with on-stage musician John Patrick Elliott is what keeps the show gripping from start to finish. It's all supported by an impeccable sound design, reminiscent of a high-budget true crime podcast. If you're already a fan of true crime, I wouldn't go into this expecting a Ted Bundy-level tale. What's memorable here is not so much the story itself, but the way the story is told. As an acting showcase, it's simply extraordinary. Jack's got the timing and the potency of these characters down to a science, but it never feels stiff or overdone. He doesn't try to look or sound exactly like a middle aged, bartending woman from Missouri, for example. Instead, he shifts his energy and physicality in a way that's transparent but can still unsettle and surprise. So even though there were so many constructs at play within this piece, I was right there, in the story 100%. It's not rare to see good theatre when you live in New York, but it is rare and a real treat to see something this innovative. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: Detailed first-hand review of KENREX at the Lucille Lortel, covering Jack Holden's acting, sound design, storytelling, and overall recommendation.
